reason: The examples describe the margins of the part, not the corolla lip itself. A lip with an undulate margin is fine. A rule would need to send 'margins undulate' to a margin class, or to the lip only when the lip is named.

A lamina can be shorter than something else. But the examples are comparisons about other parts: trichomes, 'shorter than stems' and 'shorter than culms'. A rule would need to tell comparisons ('shorter than X') from real length values, and take the bearer from the subject of the phrase.
Internodes have a diameter, and the examples give sensible values.
Sporophyll shape such as deltate or ovate-lanceolate is meaningful. 'Base cordate' is a sub-part, but the main statements are correct.
Filiform (thread-like) petals are a normal botanical description.
Winged pedicels or peduncles occur. The negated 'not winged' is handled by negation, not by this pair.
A moss seta is often twisted. Torsioned (twisted) is the right PATO sense.
Setose pedicels are a normal description. 'Setae sparse' is a different statement, but the pair is fine.
Wrong reading. '2-lobed' or '3-fid' counts the lobes of the rostellum. The rostellum lobe is not the bearer of an amount. The count belongs to the rostellum as lobed, or to a lobe-count rule.

Wrong reading. 'Seeds few' is the number of seeds, a count of the seed as a part (amount of seeds). It is not a quality of one seed. 'Has fewer parts of type' means the bearer has fewer parts of some type, not that the seeds are few.
A trilobed orchid labellum is a standard character. The French examples are also correct.
Buds can be hairy, with hairs or a hairy covering.
Quadrate cells are common in bryophyte leaf descriptions. Quadrangular is the closest PATO shape.
Wrong part. The examples describe basal laminal cells, which are rectangular. The leaf itself is not described as rectangular. The bearer should be the cell.

Fibrillose applies to leaf sheaths and bands, such as old leaf bases in palms, grasses and monocots, which fray into fibres. It is not a quality of the whole leaf. A rule would need the sheath or band to be named as the bearer.

The examples say ellipsoid. The PATO prolate term is a cell-shape value. Ellipsoid inflorescence is meaningful, but mapping ellipsoid to prolate is doubtful. A rule would need a mapping of ellipsoid to a proper 3D shape term.
'Loose mats' and 'lax' describe growth form or tuft density, and 'laxinodis' is a taxon name. A rule would need to tell habit from a name.
Concave faces or sides of an achene are a normal description.
Herbaceous (leaf-like, not membranous) sepals are a standard character.
Indurate (hardened) bracts or bract bases are meaningful.
Wrong reading. The examples count cells or rows in the alar region ('1-3 quadrate cells'). That is the number of cells in a region, not an amount of alar cells as a bearer.
The depth of a hypanthium, often as a ratio to its width, is a standard character.
Bristly receptacles are a normal description in the Asteraceae.
Petals can be sericeous (silky-hairy), usually on the outside.
Spathe dimensions such as '7-26 × 4-16 cm' are meaningful. The examples may include a length-by-width pair, and the width part is fine.
Cell diameter in µm is a normal measurement.
Spreading or divergent thorns and spines are meaningful.
Spine counts per areole in cacti are standard. Cactus spines are modified leaves.
Lobed pinnae are meaningful, as in ferns and cycads.
'Sunken' and 'impressed' are usually said of veins, stomata or glands on the lamina, not of the lamina itself. A rule would need the sunken structure named.
The number of pollen sacs per anther is a meaningful count.
Subglobose capsules are common. Spheroid is the closest PATO shape.
Spathes can have an acuminate apex. The apex is a sub-part, but the statement reads as a spathe quality.
Winged stalks or stipes are meaningful, as in ferns.
'Pale' and 'pallid' mean a light colour, which is lightness, not necessarily low saturation. A rule would need to say whether pale maps to a light colour or to low saturation.
The distance of veins from the margin or from each other is meaningful. The bearers are veins, so a vein class may fit better.
Keeled stipules are a standard character.
Erose (irregularly toothed) bract margins are meaningful.
Hairiness of the adaxial epidermis or surface is meaningful. Pilosity is the attribute and the hair types are the values.
Filiform staminodes are a normal description.
Sericeous petioles are a normal description.
'Anastomosing' means veins join to form a network. That is vein connectivity, not branchiness, which is the number of branches. A rule would need a separate term for anastomosing.
Wrong part. 'Entire' describes a margin, as in 'nearly entire in the acumen'. A trichome of the shoot axis does not have an entire margin in this sense.
Short stipules or ocreae, and a stipule shorter than the petiole, are meaningful.
Small or minute corollas are meaningful.
Free (not attached) disc glands are a meaningful description.
Wrong reading. 'Dehiscing longitudinally' is how the anther opens (dehiscence mode), not the orientation of the anther. It needs a dehiscence term.
Unequal or equal corolla lobes is a standard character. Size is used as the comparison attribute.
Straight petals or petal tips are meaningful.
Prickly pedicels are meaningful. 'Unarmed' is the negation.
Glabrous pinnae are meaningful.
Terete (round in section) roots and taproots are meaningful.
The width of a moss peristome in µm or mm is a normal measurement.
Prominent primary veins, abaxially or adaxially, are a standard character.

Wrong reading. 'With 4-6 spathes' is the number of spathes that a parent (inflorescence or plant) has. It is not an amount quality of a single spathe. The count belongs to the parent as a counted-part rule.
Lamina colour such as green is meaningful. The PATO term is the general optical quality, so a colour term would be more precise.
The colour of the abaxial epidermis or surface of a sepal is meaningful.
Papery (chartaceous) stipules are meaningful.
An oblong calyptra is a standard moss character.
The 2D shape of a utricle (elliptic, ovate) is meaningful.
